name: RT-2 Vision-Language-Action Models (Brohan et al. 2023)
observations: Source: Google DeepMind, 'RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control', Anthony Brohan et al., arXiv:2307.15818v1, 28 Jul 2023, 26 pages.

Core thesis: a large VLM pretrained on web data can become an end-to-end robot policy (a vision-language-action / VLA model) with no new architecture, by co-fine-tuning on robot trajectories plus the original Internet-scale vision-language tasks (VQA, captioning, interleaved image-text).

Key trick, actions as another language: 6-DoF end-effector delta pose (dpos xyz, drot xyz), gripper extension and a discrete terminate command are each discretized into 256 uniform bins and emitted as an 8-integer string such as 1 128 91 241 5 101 127, so actions share the token space with text.

Token binding: PaLI-X has unique tokens for integers up to 1000 so action bins map to integer tokens; PaLM-E instead overwrites its 256 least-frequently-used tokens with the action vocabulary (a form of symbol tuning). Prompt format is VQA-style: Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A: <action tokens>.

Instantiations: RT-2-PaLI-X at 5B and 55B (ViT-22B encoder plus 32B/50-layer UL2-style encoder-decoder) and RT-2-PaLM-E at 12B (ViT-4B projected into a decoder-only LLM), plus a PaLI-3B variant for the simulated Language-Table benchmark.

Co-fine-tuning is the crucial recipe detail: mixing robot data with the original web data (robot share about 50 percent for PaLI-X, 66 percent for PaLM-E) generalizes much better than robot-only fine-tuning because web concepts are not forgotten. Ablations: training from scratch is poor even at 5B; fine-tuning alone beats scratch but loses to co-fine-tuning; bigger models generalize better.
Output constraint: when prompted with a robot-action task the decoder may only sample the 256 valid action tokens, while standard vision-language tasks keep the full natural-language vocabulary.
Real-time inference: the 55B model runs in a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network at 1-3 Hz closed-loop; the 5B model reaches about 5 Hz; a 3B model reaches about 5 Hz in simulation.

Training: behavior cloning as next-token prediction. LR 1e-3 with batch 2048 for PaLI-X 5B (270K steps) and 55B (80K steps); LR 4e-4 with batch 512 for PaLM-E 12B (1M steps). Robot data is the RT-1 dataset: 13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen, 7-DoF mobile manipulator, 7 skills, language-annotated episodes.

Results over about 6k real-world trials: seen-task success is roughly comparable to RT-1, but generalization to unseen objects, backgrounds and environments is about 2x the next best baselines (RT-1, MOO) and about 6x the VC-1/R3M representation baselines. On simulated Language-Table, RT-2-PaLI-3B scores 90 +/- 10 versus LAVA 77 +/- 4, RT-1 74 +/- 13 and BC-Zero 72 +/- 3.

Emergent capabilities from web pretraining, absent from robot data: symbol understanding (move coke can near 3, push coke can on top of heart), reasoning (same-color matching, math such as move banana near the sum of two plus one, logos, nutrition, multilingual Spanish/French/German instructions), and human recognition (move coke can to person with glasses, celebrities). Best RT-2 is over 3x the best baseline on average.

Chain-of-thought variant: a few hundred extra gradient steps on data augmented with a Plan field before the Action tokens (for example: Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: 1 128 124 136 121 158 111 255) lets a single model plan in language and then act, bridging VQA and manipulation data.

Stated limitations: only semantic and visual concepts transfer, no new motor skills (physical skills stay bounded by the robot data distribution); compute cost and inference latency are the bottleneck for high-frequency control (future work: quantization, distillation); very few VLMs then offered fine-tuning APIs, so open models matter for reproduction.

Practical takeaways for building a VLA: start from a strong pretrained VLM instead of training from scratch; keep web/VLM data in the fine-tuning mixture; encode actions in the backbone's own token space rather than adding action-only heads; constrain decoding to valid action tokens; budget explicitly for inference latency and serving architecture.

name: VLA Tooling Stack for Vision-Language Robotics (2026)
observations: Hugging Face LeRobot is the most practical open stack for RT-2-style workflows: LeRobotDataset (episode-aware video/image plus state plus action datasets on the Hub), policies ACT, Diffusion, SmolVLA, pi0, pi0.5, Wall-X, X-VLA, VQ-BeT, TD-MPC (all PreTrainedPolicy subclasses), composable processors, simulated envs and real robots behind one action/observation contract, and CLIs lerobot-record, lerobot-train, lerobot-eval, lerobot-rollout, lerobot-teleoperate, lerobot-calibrate, lerobot-replay.

Fine-tuning a VLA in LeRobot is one command: lerobot-train --policy.path=lerobot/smolvla_base --dataset.repo_id=<user>/<dataset> --batch_size=64 --steps=20000 --output_dir=outputs/train/my_smolvla --policy.device=cuda (about 4 hours for 20k steps on one A100). For larger options use --policy.type=smolvla with --policy.load_vlm_weights=true, or pi0/pi05.

Parameter-efficient tuning mirrors the RT-2 idea of reusing rather than rebuilding the VLM: lerobot-train with --peft.method_type=LORA --peft.r=64 --peft.lora_alpha=64 and LR around 1e-3, roughly 10x full fine-tuning.

Data collection replaces RT-1's robot dataset: lerobot-record --robot.type=so101_follower --teleop.type=so101_leader --dataset.repo_id=<user>/record-test --dataset.num_episodes=5 --dataset.single_task="Grab the black cube", or programmatically with LeRobotDataset.create plus record_loop, save_episode and push_to_hub.

The modern answer to RT-2's 1-3 Hz serving bottleneck is Real-Time Chunking: lerobot-rollout --inference.type=rtc --inference.rtc.execution_horizon=10 --inference.rtc.max_guidance_weight=10.0 --policy.path=<user>/pi0_policy, recommended for slow large VLAs (pi0, pi0.5, SmolVLA) to keep motion smooth despite inference latency.

Hugging Face Transformers supplies the VLM backbone layer behind RT-2-style models: AutoProcessor/ProcessorMixin composes a tokenizer with an image processor, and the architecture is vision tower (CLIP or SigLIP) to multi_modal_projector to language model, with image features concatenated or replacing embeddings at image placeholders. PaliGemmaProcessor handles image/loc/seg tokens and can auto-generate labels by masking prompt tokens via token_type_ids, which fits the Q/A action-as-text format well.

OpenVLA (open 7B VLA on Open X-Embodiment) and the Open X-Embodiment dataset are the de-facto open counterparts for reproducing the co-fine-tuning recipe. Caveat: OpenVLA was not indexed in the documentation source used here, so confirm its current API and version from its GitHub repo before adopting.

Recommended practical path: record demonstrations into LeRobotDataset format, fine-tune a pretrained VLA (SmolVLA, pi0 or pi0.5, optionally LoRA) with VLM weights loaded, serve rollouts with RTC to absorb latency, and validate in simulation (LIBERO or LIBERO-plus via --env.type=libero) before real-robot trials.
